items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: one of my students said something I’ll never forget. He was a freshman, okay?

ctx.x: So I’m including you in that group, Vince, because I’ve talked to three or four people before this interview and they all went, “Ohhh, Vince man, that cat —” so you have led a remarkable career and spread a lot of positive energy over the years to a lot of people. So I want to thank you for that.

Well thank you. You know the reason is because I think if your mission is related to people and you care about what they’re doing, that’s the vibe they get. Because I always wonder, I say I’m just doing what I’m supposed to do I thought. I thought everybody did that. Because I can say that’s how clueless I really was and still am sometimes. And the thing with the syllabus too that I wrote and all of that, I said, of course with my background, and I tell people this I said, “Do you know where Viper, Kentucky is?”…

played one because everybody gets on stage once at a big recital that everybody plays on, and plays all or part of a movement of a piece and only with the trumpet players there as their audience. So anyway they’ve been on stage. But in the meantime they haven’t been in this situation where they’re getting graded for it, you know, and stuff. So I get off stage and I said, “Well, John, what are you going to play?” And he goes, “I’m going to play that there Heyden song.” And I realized where I was, you know what I…
